waypoints.name: Ebbetts Pass
waypoints.advice: 63 km in you reach Ebbetts Pass. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Markleeville, mostly downhill.

sections.advice: Arnold California → Lake Alpine is 49 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Lake Alpine → Ebbetts Pass climbs about 2663 m in 23 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Ebbetts Pass → Markleeville drops about 2663 m over 21 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Arnold California → Lake Alpine
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 49 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go — slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

scenicChapters.title: Ebbetts Pass Scenic Byway
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2663 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

ebbetts-pass-scenic-byway.story: A 94 km one-way ride from near Arnold, about 1 h 33 of riding. The stops in between: Lake Alpine and Ebbetts Pass. The highest point is about 2,650 m. Ebbetts Pass is open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

places-covacho-ahumado-abric-de-la-tenal.story: 247 km from Alacón to Alacón, about 4 h 16 of riding. The stops in between: Abrigo del Barranco Hondo, Abric de la Tenalla and back through Abrigo del Barranco Hondo. The highest point is about 1,200 m. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
